questions.q: sales has shape (3, 4): three stores in rows and four weeks in columns. What does sales.sum(axis=0) return?
options: Four values, one total per week (column)
Three values, one total per store (row)
questions.explain: The axis you name is the one that disappears. Summing over axis 0 collapses the rows, leaving one total per column.

questions.q: For x = [12, 15, 11, 18, 14, 90], the mean is about 26.7 and the median is 14.5. Why do they differ so much?
options: The mean was computed with the wrong axis
The outlier 90 pulls the mean up, while the median depends only on the middle of the sorted data
questions.explain: The mean uses every value's size, so one extreme value shifts it. The median is the middle value and is resistant to outliers.

questions.q: What does passing ddof=1 to np.std do?
options: Divides by n - 1 instead of n, giving the sample standard deviation
Rounds the result to one decimal place
Computes the standard deviation along axis 1
questions.explain: ddof is the delta degrees of freedom. ddof=1 gives the sample estimate. NumPy defaults to 0, while pandas defaults to 1.

questions.q: y = np.array([1.0, np.nan, 3.0]). Which expression returns 2.0?
questions.explain: np.mean returns nan when any value is nan. np.nanmean skips nan values, so it averages 1.0 and 3.0.

questions.q: What does the z-score (x - x.mean()) / x.std() tell you about each value?
options: How many standard deviations it is from the mean
Its correlation with the other values
questions.explain: Subtracting the mean centers the data and dividing by the standard deviation rescales it, so each value is expressed in standard deviations from the mean.
